_comment: Macro benchmark baseline: four bots replaying the standard session.
Regenerate: bot bench --rounds 120 --json benches/macro-baseline.json
Gate: CI fails if p99 exceeds 2x this value, or 5% of a tick, whichever
is larger (bot::bench::REGRESSION_FACTOR and NOISE_FLOOR_US).
The workload fields are checked, not decorative: comparing a run at a
different --rounds measures the parameters rather than the server.
HARDWARE MATTERS. These came from the machine named below; a CI runner is
different silicon and was measured at 1.65x this machine on the previous
workload. That is why the floor exists: p99 is now under half a
millisecond, and twice a number that small is inside a shared runner's
scheduling noise.
REBASELINED 2026-08-07, and again because the WORKLOAD changed rather
than the server. Two things forced it. The session used to be one
recording replayed by all four bots, which worked only while a client
could write blocks straight into the world: with real digging the first
bot to arrive takes the block and the other three ask for one that is
already air, carry nothing, and fail on the placement after it. Nightly
had been red on exactly that. Each bot now walks to its own ground and
digs before it builds, the way a player has to.
The numbers also moved for a real reason, and it is worth knowing which
part is which. p99 fell from 1414 us to 358 us and the mean from 463 us
to 63 us, mostly because the tick no longer relights chunks that already
have light: four bots joining at once asked for the same chunks, and each
of them was paying 1.38 ms a chunk for an answer the first one had
already worked out. Before that fix this workload measured a 22 ms tick;
it now measures 8.1 ms, and that worst tick is the join burst - four
players arriving in the same tick, generating and encoding terrain none
of them has seen. 16% of a 50 ms budget, once, at the start of a run.
Run-to-run spread on the reference machine, four spaced runs: p99 307,
358, 395 us, and one run at 612 us taken immediately after another
benchmark, which is contention rather than the server. Take a baseline
from a quiet machine.
_machine: dev container, AMD Ryzen 7 7800X3D, release build
